title: Le Chatelier and industrial compromise
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Chemistry (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: EQ02#t4 term and clue written for the game; EQ02#t1 term and clue written for the game; EQ02#t3 term and clue written for the game; EQ02#t2 term and clue written for the game. Questions: EQ02#N.3b, EQ02#N.5, EQ02#N.10, EQ02#N.14.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Equilibrium constant
items.clue: The value K, which only a change in temperature can alter.

items.label: Le Chatelier's principle
items.clue: When a system at equilibrium is disturbed, it shifts so as to partly oppose the change.

items.label: Catalyst
items.clue: Speeds up forward and backward reactions equally, changing neither the composition nor K.

items.label: Position of equilibrium
items.clue: The composition of the mixture in a balanced reversible reaction; it can shift left or right.

questions.stem: The hypothetical reaction D(g) + E(g) ⇌ G(g) is at equilibrium in a rigid container with [D] = 0.20 M. More D(g) is then injected, which raises [D] to 0.50 M at the moment of injection. Which statement describes [D] once equilibrium is re-established at the same temperature?

options.text: It stays at 0.50 M, its value just after the injection
It settles at a value between 0.20 M and 0.50 M
It rises to some value that is greater than 0.50 M
It returns to 0.20 M, its value before the injection

questions.explanation: Q < K, so net forward reaction uses up some D. The stress is only partly counteracted: if [D] fell all the way to 0.20 M, with less E and more G than before, Q would exceed K.

questions.stem: CH₄(g) + H₂O(g) ⇌ CO(g) + 3H₂(g). The pressure is increased, by reducing the volume, at constant temperature. What happens?

options.text: The position shifts right, giving more H₂; K is unchanged.
The position shifts left, giving less H₂; K decreases.
There is no shift, because every species is a gas.
The position shifts left, giving less H₂; K is unchanged.

questions.explanation: 2 mol of gas on the left, 4 on the right. Higher pressure favours the side with fewer moles of gas, the left. Temperature is constant, so K is unchanged.

questions.stem: A test tube holds orange potassium dichromate(VI) solution: 2CrO₄²⁻(aq) + 2H⁺(aq) ⇌ Cr₂O₇²⁻(aq) + H₂O(l). Sodium hydroxide solution is added drop by drop. What is seen, and why?

options.text: It turns yellow, because OH⁻ removes H⁺ and the position shifts left.
There is no change, because OH⁻ does not appear in the equation.
It turns a deeper orange, because the added base speeds up the forward reaction.
It turns yellow, because the alkali lowers the value of K.

questions.explanation: OH⁻ reacts with H⁺ to form water. Losing H⁺ shifts the position left, towards yellow chromate(VI).

questions.stem: Methanol is made from CO(g) + 2H₂(g) ⇌ CH₃OH(g). The forward reaction is exothermic. Plants run it at high pressure. Why does raising the pressure, by reducing the volume, increase the equilibrium yield of methanol?

options.text: K increases at high pressure, so more methanol is present at equilibrium.
The forward reaction is exothermic, so high pressure pushes the position right.
The position shifts right: the right side has fewer moles of gas.
More frequent collisions at high pressure speed up the forward reaction only.

questions.explanation: 3 mol of gas on the left, 1 on the right. Raising the pressure favours the side with fewer gas molecules, which partly opposes the change.
